the introduction of FCV will increase platinum demand but will reduce its release to the environment.

the identified resources of platinum are expected to be depleted before the end of this century, and the amount of platinum accumulated by the time platinum resources are depleted would be more than double its known resources.
platinum demand is expected to increase in all scenarios at a different rate and its identified resources would be depleted by the time platinum demand reaches the maximum.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the analysis of future platinum intentional and non- intentional flows and stocks, the assessment of its future resources and emissions and the quantification of the potential resources of platinum in secondary resources.
a better understanding of the long term impacts that the use of platinum has on its future demand, supply, release and accumulation.
the long-term impacts of the use and release of platinum on its future resources, environmental releases and accumulations in mineral waste, soils, landfill sites and building materials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the introduction of FCV will not solve the problem of platinum depletion and accumulation in the environment.
platinum is a scarce metal and its identified resources would be depleted by the time it is needed the most.

the use of platinum is increasing in different applications and its identified resources will deplete before the depletion of its identified resources and that there are potential resources of platinum in secondary material that can be used for platinum supply.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
platinum is an important resource for the future.

the future supply and demand of platinum is not only determined by its identified resources and its intentional uses, but also by its non-intentional uses, its release to the environment, the accumulation in soil, mineral waste, landfill sites and in construction materials and its recycling.
the use of platinum in FCVs is expected to decrease the release to the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the accumulation of platinum in mineral waste and other materials can be a potential future resource for platinum and should not be overlooked in the analysis of its resources and supply.
the accumulation of metals in the environment and in waste streams should be taken into account in the assessment of their future resources.
it is possible to quantify the amount of a metal accumulated in secondary materials that could be available for future supply.
